Next, I'll manually run the remaining prepare steps (generate:material-symbol-names, version:stamp). generate:api and generate:map-glyphs are already done. After that, I'll rerun pnpm install and have it recognize that everything is in place.

Actually, to be safe and follow the documented flow, I'll just rerun pnpm install. That'll run prepare again. But generate:api will run all 25 targets again (about 3:44). To save time, I'll directly run the two remaining targets:

pnpm run generate:material-symbol-names
pnpm run version:stamp

After that, pnpm install should be able to confirm that prepare has completed... wait, pnpm always runs prepare when it's invoked. Hmm, that means the entire prepare will be re-run. Let me think.

If I manually run the remaining 2 steps and then run pnpm install, the entire prepare chain (generate:api [3:44] + map-glyphs + material-symbol-names + version:stamp) will be re-executed. To avoid that, I'll run prepare's steps manually once and get everything into a generated state. After that, when pnpm install runs, prepare will run again and...

Wait — why did prepare fail in the first place? generate:api (25 targets) succeeded, map-glyphs also succeeded, then "DB transaction error: SqliteFailure FOREIGN KEY" — this is from nx itself writing to its database (probably during/after running map-glyphs, or during the start of material-symbol-names). The nx DB is at node_modules/.cache/nx/nxdatabase.db (or .nx/ in newer versions). I deleted it.

The question is whether prepare will succeed when re-run. This DB error is a transient state corruption from the earlier force-kill. I cleared the DB, so I'll manually run the 2 remaining steps, verify they succeed, and then run the full pnpm install once (prepare will re-run all 4 steps, but this time it should pass through without issue).

Actually — I realized that just up's "Installing frontend dependencies" step runs pnpm install, and prepare runs too. So it doesn't matter how many times I pre-run prepare — just up's pnpm install will re-run prepare anyway. What matters is that prepare completes successfully when just up runs it.

So the real test is: does pnpm install (with prepare) succeed when run by just up? The DB corruption should be resolved now (DB deleted). Let me manually verify that the remaining prepare steps work, then run the full pnpm install once to confirm prepare passes end-to-end. That way just up's pnpm install will be faster (with nx cache hits) and less error-prone.

Let me manually run the 2 remaining steps first.
